title: Roman Number to Integer and vice versa
problemStatement: Convert a Roman numeral to an integer and an integer to a Roman numeral.
intuition: Roman to integer: a smaller symbol immediately before a larger one is subtracted. Integer to Roman: greedily take the largest value that fits, using a table that already includes the subtractive pairs.

approaches.title: Roman -> integer
approaches.idea: Compare each symbol with the next; subtract when smaller.

approaches.title: Integer -> Roman
approaches.idea: Greedy over a descending table that includes CM, CD, XC, XL, IX, IV.
approaches.whyWorks: Including the subtractive pairs in the table makes plain greedy correct.

edgeCases: Subtractive pairs at the string end
Values above 3999 are undefined in classic Roman
commonMistakes: Hard-coding subtraction rules instead of comparing with the next symbol
Omitting the subtractive entries from the greedy table
patternRecognition: Greedy works when the "coin system" is canonical — Roman values are
followUps: Why is greedy correct here but not for arbitrary coin sets?
interviewInsight: The connection to the coin-change greedy correctness question is a great thing to raise.
